data.narrative:
Swift Solar, a Series C climate and energy company, is evaluated here against a peer set of three same-stage, same-sector private companies (KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy) plus broader comparable data from one public company in the sector.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $52.7M in total capital raised as a proxy baseline, applying a 1.7x multiplier typical for Series C-to-next-stage step-ups, yielding $90M. Peer-median analysis examines the three identified comparables, which traded at a median valuation of $1.0B with a range of $700M to $3.0B, directly implying a $1.0B valuation for Swift Solar on comparable metrics.

The triangulated analysis across both methods produces a valuation range of $76M to $1.1B, with a median estimate of $545M. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty inherent in frontier-tech venture valuations at this stage. Stage-progression yields the conservative bound based on capital-raised extrapolation, while peer-median anchors to observable market comparables but is sensitive to the small sample size and heterogeneity within the peer set—KoBold Metals trades at 4.3x the floor set by Amogy. Key uncertainties include technology validation timelines, path to commercialization specificity, and the sustainability of peer valuations given sector volatility.
